saints.name: St. Maurice and the Theban Legion
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: A legion of Christian soldiers who, led by their commander Maurice, chose death rather than turn their swords against the innocent or deny their faith…
biography: According to the letter of Eucherius, Bishop of Lyon, written about 450, the Theban Legion was a body of Christian soldiers recruited at Thebes in Egypt and sent by the Emperor Maximian into Gaul against the rebels of Burgundy. When the army reached Agaunum in the Alps, now Saint-Maurice in the Valais, the legion refused to sacrifice to the gods and to turn its weapons against fellow Christians.

Under their commander Maurice, together with Candidus, Innocent, and Exuperius, the soldiers stood firm while the legion was twice decimated, every tenth man put to the sword, and was at last cut down entire, about the year 287. Their confession, recorded by Eucherius, was that they owed the emperor their service but God their innocence.

In the following century Theodore, Bishop of Octodurum, built a basilica over the martyrs' relics, and on the site rose the abbey of Saint-Maurice, founded in 515 on land given by King Sigismund of Burgundy and still occupied today. As soldiers who chose death rather than an impious order, Maurice and his legionaries are patrons of soldiers and infantry and of the Alpine lands.
saints.knownFor: Their refusal to persecute fellow Christians, sealed by martyrdom.
